ai.analysis: Gold is up 0.67% at 4,021 because the rates picture keeps improving: the 10-year TIPS real yield is 2.64%, down 10bp from 2.74% five sessions ago, the 2-year is off 9bp to 4.65%, and the dollar has slipped about 1.2% from its Oct 14 high of 102.95 to around 101.5. The catch is that gold had all of that last week and still lost about 4%, closing at 3,995.81 for its first sub-$4,000 close since mid-July - seven sessions of gold ignoring its master driver, which is why this is a neutral call and not a buy. The Fed is the single bearish layer and it is the loudest one: Wednesday is a ~90% hold with zero cuts priced, a December hike sits at 72-78%, and core PCE Thursday is expected near 3.1% with Michigan inflation expectations up at 4.7% - that is a hawkish backdrop, even though the rates themselves have been easing. What is quietly helping is that December hike odds have come down from roughly 90% on Friday to about 80% today, which is exactly what pulled yields and the dollar lower and let gold bounce off a three-month low. Reclaim 4,100 and the bullish stack earns the benefit of the doubt; lose Friday's 3,975.65 low and the bounce is finished - and nothing really settles before Wednesday 2:00pm.

headline: NEUTRAL - the stack is BUY-SIDE (+4: real yields -10bp, 2Y -9bp, dollar off its high, crude near 4-year highs) but gold lost 4% last week doing the opposite, and a December hike stays ~80% priced into Wednesday's FOMC.

mind.line: Rates, the dollar and crude all say buy, and the tape has ignored them for seven sessions - that is no edge, not a fade. It becomes a buy on a reclaim of 4,100 that holds while real yields stay down; it becomes a sell on acceptance back below Friday's 3,975.65. A hot core PCE Thursday, or December hike odds pushing back above 90%, kills the bullish case outright.
